pr_title: Allow specifying code ranges for autocorrect
pr_body:
Adds command line flags that when present will filter autocorrections performed

Fixes https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/10930

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].
* [x] Commit message starts with `[Fix #issue-number]` (if the related issue exists).
* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

[1]: https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/
pr_comments: @rafaelfranca tagging you here in case someone from Shopify is interested in providing feedback (as it's related to LSP).
@bbatsov Thanks for the feedback! Made the updates and also added a section to the docs

Thank you @HeroProtagonist!

I am not sure if I can explain it well, but I will try to write my thoughts anyway.

Overall, I honestly think that my proposal at https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/10930 may have been too subtle. 

Of course it would be nice to have the ability to specify a range at the CLI or `RuboCop::Runner` API level. This is because this is probably the only way to realize a repetitive correction loop process while specifying a range in one instruction. But, on the other hand, I don't think there are that many use cases to require this feature. If it does not interfere with the growth of RuboCop, I would be happy to add it, but if this feature would make RuboCop more complicated, I think it would be better to give up adding this feature.


I am sorry for suggesting this, but after developing the editor extension since then, I realized that I could not provide a good editing experience if RuboCop was controlled from an external process via CLI. So I stopped implementing the Language Server in JavaScript and rewrote the Language Server from scratch in Ruby with using RuboCop's internal API.

- https://github.com/r7kamura/vscode-ruby-light
  - VSCode extension + Language Server implementation in JavaScript
  - Made in the early days
- https://github.com/r7kamura/rucoa
  - Language Server implementation in Ruby
  - Made later

This is the main reason why I have not implemented this CLI options until today, even though it was agreed upon in the Issue.

When implemented in Ruby, RuboCop's internal API can be used to retrieve corrected text from `RuboCop::Cop::Offense` with correction range information using `Parser::Source::TreeRewriter#as_replacements`. 

```ruby
offense.corrector.as_replacements
```

With this API, we can achieve most of what we want to do about range specification, by checking whether the range obtained from `offense` is within the range specified by the editor, limitation to only the range can be achieved, although not perfectly. Here is the code I actually use in my Language Server implementation:

- https://github.com/r7kamura/rucoa/blob/4ec510a66e0cd928c764712788d504800d2edebd/lib/rucoa/handlers/text_document_range_formatting_handler.rb#L57-L65
- https://github.com/whitequark/parser/blob/d0c86fe3d149a9cb6484ed094ffdf8595f2205cc/lib/parser/source/tree_rewriter.rb#L265-L283

In fact, other Ruby-made Lanauge Servers also use this method. For example, this is the case with ruby-lsp, which is developed by Shopify:

- https://github.com/Shopify/ruby-lsp/blob/d99eaf4107ede941cebdbf324f10525e8eacc67c/lib/ruby_lsp/requests/support/rubocop_diagnostic.rb#L93

> although not perfectly

This may be an important topic for this Pull Request. The reason why I wrote it this way is because the logic just described above does not work perfectly in cases where one correction would create a new offense.

The advantage of the CLI option added in this Pull Request is that the iterative correction process using `RuboCop::Runner#do_inspection_loop` will be executed so that the correction is completed at once.

However, it is an occasional problem, and the cases where users want to specify a range are very rare (in the case of the Ruby-made Language Server, it is probably only used for `textDocument/rangeFormatting`), and even if it does occur, it can be resolved by re-running the formatting command several times.

That's why I said:

> I don't think there are that many use cases to require this feature.

at the beginning of this comment.

When I first tried to suggest this, I thought that [Quick Fix](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/111689/185023861-e4bf6237-4cd6-4439-8497-b843dc3ea2c3.gif) would need this feature, but then I realized that the editor actually needs to fix things pretty fast and this feature would not work. At the initial stage of diagnosing the offenses, the server needs to return the corrected text to the editor along with the offense, so that when the user presses the button, the correction is completed in an instant. So it is impractical to run autocorrect again when the button is pressed, therefore this CLI option cannot be used in this case.

---

I also have a question about the suggested implementation. If a new offense occurs as a result of autocorrection while specifying a range, how should it be fixed, and would the suggested implementation unintentionally modify code that was originally out of the range?
Seems we won't be moving forward with this, so I'll close it.

issue_context.title: CLI options for specifying source code range
issue_context.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I would like to have CLI options to autocorrect offenses by specifying a source code range like this:

```
rubocop \
  --autocorrect \
  --start-line 1 \
  --start-column 2 \
  --last-line 3 \
  --last-column 4 \
  foo.rb
```

This is not often used directly by humans, but mainly for program use, such as editor integrations. I'm creating a VSCode extension for Ruby and thought it would be nice to have this feature in its development.

- https://github.com/r7kamura/vscode-ruby-light

For example, the [Language Server Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/) has the following specifications:

- DocumentRangeFormatting
- Diagnostics & Quick Fix

This feature can be used to provide VSCode with the ability to fix only certain offenses like this:

![diagnostics](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/111689/185023861-e4bf6237-4cd6-4439-8497-b843dc3ea2c3.gif)

![184560748-a2057574-78e3-41df-956b-901d20627be4](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/111689/185023921-bff195b3-2b74-42f2-9647-4896f36bbe4d.gif)

## Describe the solution you'd like

The implementation should not be difficult. All we need to do is to filter the collected offenses by the specified range. (Maybe at `RuboCop::Runner` or somewhere)

## Describe alternatives you've considered

The demo above appears to work well, but in fact it is realized in a very dirty way and does not work well in many cases. If RuboCop provided CLI options to specify a range, we would be able to achieve the functionality described above.

For now, I am rewriting the entire file once with `rubocop --autocorrect`, then converting the diff to an array of patches and applying only the patches in the range. This is the same method used in other editor integration with RuboCop, such as [vscode-ruby](https://github.com/rubyide/vscode-ruby).

This method has the flaw that it does not work well when the offense and patch locations are far apart, because it works depending on the location of the corrector, not on the location of the offense. For example, a reordering type of Cop, such as `Bundler/OrderedGems`, will fail with this method.

review_comments: As this is a public API it'd be good to document the purpose of `range`.
